doc_summary: A cross-post (Sam Marks is not a co-author) introducing Petri, an open-source automated auditing framework where AI agents run multi-turn scenarios against target models from seed instructions. It argues automation is needed because manual alignment evaluation is engineering-heavy and cannot cover the vast space of possible misbehaviors.

items.claim: Prefers broad automated auditing across many behaviors over hand-testing a handful of behaviors because the space of potential misalignments is vast and narrow testing misses much of what matters.
items.quote: There aren't good tools to automate this work, and the space of potential misalignments is vast. If you can only test a handful of behaviors, you'll likely miss much of what matters.

items.claim: In a setup, use realistic multi-turn scenarios with simulated environments and affordances instead of single-shot prompts because misaligned behavior emerges with wide-ranging deployment affordances.
items.quote: Petri enables researchers to test hypotheses about model behavior in minutes, using AI agents to explore target models across realistic multi-turn scenarios.

items.claim: Motivated by growing deployment affordances expanding the surface area for misalignment, which exceeds what manual testing can cover.
items.quote: AI models are becoming more capable and are being deployed with wide-ranging affordances across more domains, increasing the surface area where misaligned behaviors might emerge.

items.claim: Chooses what to test by targeting a diverse set of risk-relevant behaviors (deception, oversight subversion, whistleblowing, misuse cooperation, situational awareness, scheming, self-preservation, reward hacking) via many seed instructions.
items.quote: When applied to 14 frontier models with 111 seed instructions, Petri successfully elicited a broad set of misaligned behaviors including autonomous deception, oversight subversion, whistleblowing, and cooperation with human misuse.

items.claim: Treats auditing agents as a fast, useful signal source whose flags of misbehavior are reliable enough to act on, preferring quick hypothesis-testing over exhaustive manual validation.
items.quote: Our earlier work on alignment auditing agents found these methods can reliably flag misaligned behaviors, providing useful signal quickly.

items.claim: Frames the evaluation pipeline as environment simulation, running models, reading transcripts, and aggregating results, and automates from simulation through initial transcript analysis.
items.quote: Petri automates a large part of the safety evaluation process—from environment simulation through to initial transcript analysis—making comprehensive audits possible with minimal researcher effort.

items.claim: Uses auditing agents to evaluate situational awareness alongside other behaviors in system cards, treating evaluation awareness as one of the audited behaviors.
items.quote: We used them in the Claude 4 and Claude Sonnet 4.5 System Cards to evaluate behaviors such as situational awareness, scheming, and self-preservation

items.claim: Prefers lowering the engineering cost of building evaluations so more researchers can audit, because manual evaluation construction is a bottleneck.
items.quote: Building an alignment evaluation requires substantial engineering effort: setting up environments, writing test cases, implementing scoring mechanisms.
